protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: PASS: Real CWE-78 OS command injection in NodejsFunction Docker bundling. Source: package.json dependency version strings for nodeModules (BIC: PackageJsonManager.getVersions; later extractDependencies in packages/aws-cdk-lib/aws-lambda-nodejs/lib/util.ts:135). Interpolation: JSON.stringify of those versions is placed inside a single-quoted echo that is chained into a bash -c command (BIC createBundlingCommand in packages/@aws-cdk/aws-lambda-nodejs/lib/bundling.ts; at v2.259.0 OsCommand.writeJson -> write returns `echo '${data}' > "${filePath}"` at packages/aws-cdk-lib/aws-lambda-nodejs/lib/bundling.ts:628, used from dockerFileOps writeJson of {dependencies}). Sink: DockerBundler command ['bash','-c', bundlingCommand] (BIC DockerBundler ~line 294; v2.259.0 Bundling.command ~line 238) inside a container with host bind mounts (AssetStaging BUNDLING_INPUT_DIR/OUTPUT_DIR). A version containing a single quote terminates the echo argument and injects metacharacters. GHSA-vcrf-j523-4mrf is not withdrawn; CVE-2026-13760 CNA state is PUBLISHED (AMZN) with affected AWS CDK 0 < 2.260.0; vendor bulletin 2026-050-AWS matches. Not a false-positive advisory.

findings: Advisory GHSA-vcrf-j523-4mrf / CVE-2026-13760 is a real, published OS command injection (CWE-78) in aws-cdk-lib NodejsFunction Docker bundling when nodeModules is set; GHSA withdrawn_at is null and CVE.org CNA state is PUBLISHED.

Root cause is interpolating JSON-serialized dependency version strings inside a single-quoted echo that is executed via bash -c in the bundling container, so a version containing `'` breaks out of the shell argument.

Atomic BIC is PR #9632 member 1a25fc6d99713313a21b65633f191b2307fa1d32, which replaced a safe fs.writeFileSync of the dummy package.json with the unsafe echo interpolation; immediate parent 0b60c499c54ca35dd18e59b47f6a1fb63870cbe9 lacks that mechanism.

Public mainline carrier is squash 276c322780a9a8c9c6e569509a90ba0a7bec0879, first contained in v1.60.0 and still present at v2.259.0 via later OsCommand.writeJson/write; later moves/refactors are not the BIC.
Direct fix baa9e1dff469306cc23b8f4bd232d703f98bf68a (PR #38133) applies posixShellEscape at OsCommand.write and is first released in v2.260.0.
BIC authorship is wholly human (Jonathan Goldwasser) with no AI/bot/generator markers, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
